threads.body: `prepare_tool_definitions()` can return an empty list (e.g., when `tools` contains no function-type entries). In that case, this code still sets `llm_invocation.tool_definitions` which can result in emitting an empty `gen_ai.tool.definitions` attribute instead of omitting it. Consider only setting `tool_definitions` when the prepared list is non-empty (or adjust `prepare_tool_definitions` to return `None` when no supported tools are found).

+from opentelemetry.sdk._logs import LoggerProvider
+from opentelemetry.sdk._logs.export import BatchLogRecordProcessor
+from opentelemetry.sdk.metrics import MeterProvider
+from opentelemetry.sdk.metrics.export import PeriodicExportingMetricReader
+from opentelemetry.sdk.trace import TracerProvider

+
+# Configure tracing
+trace.set_tracer_provider(TracerProvider())
+span_processor = BatchSpanProcessor(OTLPSpanExporter())
+trace.get_tracer_provider().add_span_processor(span_processor)

+# Configure logging
+_logs.set_logger_provider(LoggerProvider())
+_logs.get_logger_provider().add_log_record_processor(
+    BatchLogRecordProcessor(OTLPLogExporter())
+)

+# Configure metrics
+metrics.set_meter_provider(
+    MeterProvider(
+        metric_readers=[
+            PeriodicExportingMetricReader(
+                OTLPMetricExporter(),
+            ),
+        ]
+    )
+)
+
+
+@tool
+def multiply(a: float, b: float) -> float:
+    """Multiply two numbers together."""
+    return a * b
+
+
+@tool
+def add(a: float, b: float) -> float:
+    """Add two numbers together."""
+    return a + b
+
+
+TOOLS = [multiply, add]
+TOOLS_BY_NAME = {t.name: t for t in TOOLS}
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    LangChainInstrumentor().instrument()
+
+    llm = ChatOpenAI(
+        model="gpt-3.5-turbo",
+        temperature=0.1,
+        max_tokens=100,
+        top_p=0.9,
+        seed=100,
+    )
+    llm_with_tools = llm.bind_tools(TOOLS)

+    messages = [HumanMessage(content="What is (3 * 4) + 7?")]

+            tool_output = selected_tool.invoke(tool_call["args"])

+                    content=json.dumps(tool_output),
+                    tool_call_id=tool_call["id"],
+                )
+            )
+
+        response = llm_with_tools.invoke(messages)
+        messages.append(response)
+
+    print("Final answer:", response.content)
+
+    LangChainInstrumentor().uninstrument()

replies.body:
Yes, it's necessary. `invocation.arguments` is typed `AttributeValue | None`, which doesn't accept dict. The block converts the structured inputs: dict to a JSON string, falling back to the
  plain input_str: str. Passing Any directly would be a type violation and would break span attribute setting at runtime when inputs is a dict.

serializing to string is not right either.`AttributeValue` is not the right type for tool.arguments, it should be `opentelemetry.util.types.AnyValue` that accepts `Mapping[str, "AnyValue"]` and could be either cast or transformed from`inputs`. Note - input_str should be deserialized if `inputs` are not provided 

https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai/blob/6967795c5ceeb77357ca4f3dfc9a512496fb9a11/docs/gen-ai/gen-ai-spans.md?plain=1#L858-L860

> It's expected to be an object - in case a serialized string is available
to the instrumentation, the instrumentation SHOULD do the best effort to
deserialize it to an object
